skill.name: convex-backup
skill.description: Set up Convex backups and run a restore DRILL that proves recovery — snapshot, restore into a throwaway preview, assert the data came back — plus a schedule matched to your RPO and a gated recovery runbook.
skill.summary: Export Convex snapshots, verify recovery in a disposable deployment, and plan backup retention.
skill.author: convex

security_audit.summary: All seven alerts misidentify Markdown inline code as shell backtick execution. The workflow documents real Convex CLI operations, and restoring sensitive production data into a preview or personal development deployment can cross access boundaries. No evidence of prompt injection or a hardcoded third-party destination was found.

remediation.issue: Sensitive snapshots can be restored to preview or personal development deployments without a destination access check.
remediation.suggestion: Require approval for the exact source and destination before export and restore. Use sanitized test data or a restricted, organization-controlled deployment with production-equivalent access controls and verified cleanup.

finding_verdicts.reason: Markdown backticks delimit a documented Convex export command and an optional file storage flag. The delimiters do not execute the command or substitute its output.
The backticks format an example export command in scheduling advice. The line does not contain executable CI configuration or shell command substitution.
The backticks format the name of a deployment key environment variable. They do not read the variable, reveal its value, or run a command.
The backticks display the Convex CLI preview creation command. Creating a preview is an intentional workflow operation, not execution caused by the delimiters.
The backticks format an import command and CLI flag names. The replace operation can overwrite target data if run, but it is not backtick execution.
The backticks format MCP tool names for row counts and record checks. They do not invoke a shell or evaluate a command.
The backticks display a production restore command for a gated recovery runbook. The step calls for reporting that command, not running it during the drill.

semantic_findings.title: Sensitive Data Restored to Nonproduction Deployments
semantic_findings.description: The workflow can copy a production snapshot, including stored files when selected, into a preview or personal development deployment. Without verifying destination access, the drill can expose records and files to people or services without production access.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The workflow explicitly imports the original snapshot and permits a personal development fallback. It does not require sanitization or verification of who can access the destination.

content.user_title: Back Up Convex and Verify Recovery
content.value_statement: A Convex snapshot alone does not show that you can recover your data. Restore it into a separate deployment, check critical records, and plan future backups.
actual_capabilities: Export a Convex deployment as a ZIP snapshot, with optional inclusion of stored files.
Recommend an export schedule and retention window based on acceptable data loss.
Deploy the current code to a disposable preview and restore the snapshot there.
Check restored table counts and sample records using Convex MCP tools.
Report the drill result and document a guarded production recovery procedure.
limitations: Preview creation requires a Preview Deploy Key on an eligible paid plan.
The skill recommends a schedule but does not install CI or cron jobs.
Record spot checks do not verify every row or stored file.
Restoring an older snapshot to production can discard writes made after the snapshot.

use_cases.title: Test a First Backup
use_cases.description: Export a development deployment and check that key tables and sample records return after a separate restore.

use_cases.title: Plan Backup Frequency
use_cases.description: Choose a backup interval and retention period based on the team's acceptable data loss.

use_cases.title: Rehearse Incident Recovery
use_cases.description: Verify recovery in an approved nonproduction deployment and document the production restore approval and data loss caveat.

prompt_templates.title: Plan My First Backup
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how to back up my Convex development deployment. Identify the source and tell me whether to include stored files. Do not run commands yet.
prompt_templates.scenario: First backup with no changes or exports yet

prompt_templates.title: Choose an Export Schedule
prompt_templates.prompt: We can lose at most four hours of changes. Recommend a Convex export schedule, retention period, and storage location we control.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Test Restore
prompt_templates.prompt: Confirm my development source and the approved disposable target before exporting or importing. Check restored table counts and sample records against the source. Report which checks passed.

prompt_templates.title: Review Recovery Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a recovery drill using an approved snapshot and an access-restricted test deployment. Report verification results and draft a production runbook with approval and data loss warnings. Do not restore production.

output_examples.input: Run a drill with our development snapshot in the approved disposable preview.
output: Drill passed: The snapshot was restored to the approved preview.
The Orders table matched the source count of 240 rows, and the sampled records matched.

output_examples.input: Report the drill outcome when the restored Orders table is empty.
output: Drill failed: The restored Orders table had zero rows, but the source had 240.
Check the snapshot contents and the selected import target before repeating the drill.

best_practices: Confirm the exact source and an approved, separate restore target before running commands.
Use sanitized data when possible and restrict access to snapshots and restored copies.
Record baseline counts for critical tables and delete local snapshot copies after the drill.
anti_patterns: Treating a successful export as proof that recovery works.
Using production or a shared development deployment as the drill target.
Committing a snapshot or leaving it in an unapproved storage location.

faq.question: Does the restore drill change production?
faq.answer: No. The drill targets a separate preview or development deployment. Any production restore is a separate operation that requires approval.

faq.question: Can I run a drill without preview access?
faq.answer: Use a fresh, approved development deployment. Do not copy sensitive data there unless the destination meets your access requirements.

faq.question: Are stored files included in the snapshot?
faq.answer: Only if you enable the file storage option on export.

faq.question: How is a restore verified?
faq.answer: The drill checks row counts and samples records in critical tables. It compares against source counts where available.

faq.question: Does this replace Convex platform backups?
faq.answer: No. It adds a portable backup copy that you control alongside platform backups.

faq.question: How often should I export?
faq.answer: Set the interval based on how much recent data you can afford to lose. Keep enough restore points for your recovery needs.
